questions.question: The elections to the Panchayati Raj institutions are conducted by the ________.
questions.solution:
The State Election Commission is responsible for conducting, supervising, and controlling elections to the Panchayati Raj institutions.
  • Article 243K: This article mandates the creation of the State Election Commission for every state.
  • Difference: While the Election Commission of India (ECI) handles Parliament and State Assembly elections, the State Election Commission is independent and dedicated to local bodies.

questions.question: How many fundamental duties are provided in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties provided in the Constitution of India under Article 51A.
  • History: Originally, 10 duties were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
  • Latest Addition: The 11th duty, regarding education for children, was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

questions.question: In September 2022, which legislative assembly withdrew a bill aimed at prohibiting the movement of stray cattle on roads and public places in urban areas of the state, months after it was passed?
questions.solution:
In September 2022, the Gujarat Legislative Assembly withdrew the 'Gujarat Cattle Control (Keeping and Moving) in Urban Areas Bill'.
  • Reason: The withdrawal followed massive protests by the cattle-rearing community (Maldharis) across the state.
  • Context: The bill had sought to regulate and prohibit the movement of stray cattle on public roads in urban centers to prevent accidents.

questions.question: In which year was the Indian Parliamentary Group established?
questions.solution:
The Indian Parliamentary Group (IPG) was established in 1949.
  • Status: It is an autonomous body whose membership is open to all current and former members of Parliament.
  • Objective: It serves to promote personal contacts between MPs and to facilitate the exchange of ideas with other parliaments globally.

questions.question: Which of the following is a right under Article 300A?
questions.solution:
Article 300A provides for the Right to Property, stating that 'no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.'
  • Legal Right: Originally a Fundamental Right (Article 31), it was turned into a Legal/Constitutional Right by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
  • Impact: While no longer a Fundamental Right, it still protects citizens from arbitrary state seizure of land without legal backing.

questions.question: Article 19 of the Indian Constitution provides for how many types of freedoms?
questions.solution:
Article 19 of the Indian Constitution provides 6 types of freedoms to all citizens.
  • The Freedoms: Speech and expression, peaceful assembly, forming associations/unions, free movement, residence, and profession/trade.
  • Note: Originally there were 7, but the Right to Property was removed by the 44th Amendment.

questions.question: Which branch of the government is responsible for implementing laws and policies?
questions.solution:
The Executive is the branch of government responsible for implementing and enforcing laws and policies made by the legislature.
  • Composition: It includes the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and the permanent bureaucracy.
  • Function: It manages the daily administration of the state and carries out the will of the Parliament.

questions.question: The real executive power is vested in the Council of Ministers with the _____________ as its head.
questions.solution:
While the President is the head of state, real executive power is vested in the Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister as its head.
  • De Facto Head: The Prime Minister is the actual executive head, whereas the President is the nominal (de jure) head.
  • Accountability: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: When, for the first time, did the Election Commission of India become a multi-member body?
questions.solution:
The Election Commission of India first became a multi-member body in 1989.
  • Change: On October 16, 1989, the President appointed two more election commissioners to cope with the increased work due to the reduction of the voting age.
  • Current Status: After being a single-member body again briefly, it has been a multi-member body (1 CEC and 2 ECs) continuously since 1993.

questions.question: The fundamental duty of a parent or guradian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of 6 and ______.
questions.solution:
The 11th Fundamental Duty requires parents/guardians to provide education opportunities to children between the age of 6 and 14 years.
  • Consistency: This age bracket aligns with Article 21A (Fundamental Right) and Article 45 (DPSP).
  • Duty: It emphasizes that the responsibility for a child's education lies not just with the state, but also with the family.

questions.question: The executive power of the Union is vested in the:
questions.option_1: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
questions.option_2: Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister
questions.solution:
According to Article 53, the executive power of the Union is vested in the President.
  • Exercise of Power: These powers are exercised by the President either directly or through officers subordinate to him.
  • Note: In practice, these powers are exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the PM.

questions.question: The Constitution of India is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic with a ______________ system of government.
questions.solution:
The Indian Constitution establishes a Parliamentary system of government.
  • Feature: This system is characterized by the close relationship between the executive and the legislature.
  • Responsibility: The executive is drawn from the legislature and is accountable to it for its actions and policies.

questions.question: What is the minimum quorum required in the Lok Sabha so that it can transact any business?
questions.option_1: One-fifth of the total number of Members of the House
questions.option_2: One-tenth of the total number of Members of the House
questions.option_3: One-fourth of the total number of Members of the House
questions.option_4: One-third of the total number of Members of the House
questions.solution:
The Quorum (minimum attendance) required for the Lok Sabha to conduct business is one-tenth of the total membership.
  • Article 100: This provision ensures that a representative portion of the House is present for decision-making.
  • Calculation: For the Lok Sabha, this is roughly 55 members. If the quorum is not met, the Speaker must adjourn the House.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the voting age reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
questions.solution:
The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, which reduced the voting age from 21 to 18, was passed in 1988.
  • Implementation: It came into effect in 1989.
  • Article 326: This amendment modified Article 326 to expand the democratic base and involve youth in the electoral process.

questions.question: The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed in Lok Sabha on ________.
questions.solution:
The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed in the Lok Sabha on March 25, 2022.
  • Unification: The primary purpose of this bill was to unify the three existing municipal corporations (North, South, and East Delhi) into a single body.
  • Reasoning: The government cited financial difficulties and administrative inefficiency as the reasons for the merger.

questions.question: The 11th Fundamental Duty was added to Indian Constitution in which year?
questions.solution:
The 11th Fundamental Duty was added to the Indian Constitution in 2002.
  • Amendment: It was introduced by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.
  • Content: It pertains to the duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their ward aged 6–14.

questions.question: In November 2022, the Supreme Court upheld the validity of the 103 constitutional amendment providing _______ per cent reservation to people belonging to economically weaker section (EWS).
questions.solution:
The 103rd Amendment Act, 2019 provides 10 per cent reservation in jobs and educational institutions to the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).
  • Supreme Court Ruling: In November 2022, a 5-judge bench upheld the validity of this reservation by a 3:2 majority.
  • Articles: It amended Article 15 and Article 16 to allow for reservation based on economic criteria alone.

questions.question: In India the residuary powers to legislate any matter that is NOT mentioned in the three federal lists lies with the _____________.
questions.solution:
In India, the Residuary Powers (subjects not listed in the Union, State, or Concurrent lists) are vested in the Union Legislature (Parliament).
  • Article 248: This article gives Parliament the exclusive power to make laws on residuary subjects.
  • Global Context: This follows the Canadian model, unlike the US or Australia, where residuary powers rest with the states.

questions.question: When expenditure exceeds revenue, the budget is said to be in _______.
questions.solution:
A budget is said to be in Deficit when the total expenditure exceeds the total revenue during a fiscal year.
  • Fiscal Deficit: This is the difference between total expenditure and total receipts (excluding borrowings).
  • Contrast: A Surplus occurs when revenue exceeds expenditure, while a balanced budget is when both are equal.

questions.question: Which of the following bills can be initiated only in the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
A Money Bill can be initiated ONLY in the Lok Sabha.
  • Article 110: Defines what constitutes a Money Bill (taxes, borrowing, consolidated fund, etc.).
  • Speaker's Role: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final authority to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill or not.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Citizenship Act passed by the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:
The Citizenship Act was passed by the Indian Parliament in 1955.
  • Provisions: It details the five ways to acquire citizenship: Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, and Incorporation of territory.
  • Amendments: This act has been amended several times, most notably in 1986, 2003, 2005, 2015, and 2019.

questions.question: Every law enacted by the government has to be in conformity with the ________________.
questions.solution:
Every law enacted by the government must be in conformity with the Constitution.
  • Supreme Law: The Constitution is the Grundnorm (basic law) of India; any law that violates its provisions can be declared null and void by the judiciary.
  • Judicial Review: Under Articles 13, 32, and 226, courts check the constitutional validity of laws.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the recognition of the right to education as a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution:
Article 21A of the Constitution recognizes the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right.
  • Compulsory: It mandates the state to provide free and compulsory education to all children in the 6–14 age group.
  • Introduction: This was enacted via the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 and implemented via the RTE Act, 2009.

questions.question: The news print sector in our country is governed by which order from the following?
questions.solution:
The newsprint sector in India is regulated by the Newsprint Control Order, 2004.
  • Purpose: This order was issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
  • Regulation: It governs the registration, production, and distribution of newsprint to ensure its availability to newspaper publishers.

questions.question: Under the Constitution of India, the Constitutional Head of the Executive of the Union is the _________.
questions.solution:
The President is the Constitutional Head of the Executive of the Union.
  • Symbolic Role: All executive actions of the Government of India are formally taken in the name of the President.
  • Comparison: He is the first citizen of India and symbolizes the unity and integrity of the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following can alter the boundary of a state or change its name?
questions.solution:
The Parliament has the power to alter the boundary of a state or change its name.
  • Article 3: This article empowers Parliament to form new states, increase or decrease area, and alter boundaries/names.
  • Simple Majority: Such changes can be made by a simple majority in Parliament, although the affected state's legislature must be consulted (their opinion is not binding).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with amendment in the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Article 368 of the Constitution deals with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure therefor.
  • Part XX: This article constitutes the entire Part XX of the Constitution.
  • Rigidity vs. Flexibility: It ensures that the Constitution can evolve while maintaining its essential 'Basic Structure'.

questions.question: Fundamental Rights are mentioned in which part of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution of India.
  • Magna Carta: Part III (Articles 12 to 35) is often described as the 'Magna Carta of India'.
  • Protection: These rights are guaranteed to all citizens to protect them against the arbitrary use of power by the state.
